page.title: Best 4 Channel Dash Cam Under $300 (2026): What Each Costs With Its Parking Kit
page.desc: Six 4-channel dash cams that sold for $300 or less on 2026-11-21: what each of the four cameras sees, resolution per channel, GPS, and whether the camera plus its maker's hardwire kit for parking mode still fits under $300.
page.answer: Short answer. The best 4 channel dash cam under $300 is the Vantrue N5S: front, rear and two cabin cameras, all four on Sony STARVIS 2 sensors. Its hardwire kit for parking mode costs $29.99 and takes it past $300; for front, rear and both sides, the Rexing R4-RD includes the kit at $279.99.

page.after:
What the differences mean

Every camera in the table is one its maker sells as 4-channel, meaning four cameras recording at the same time (the count is Vantrue's, Botslab's and Rexing's own). Each sold for $300 or less on 2026-11-21: rival prices are the makers' US stores, and ours are the price through our link. Left out for being just over the line: the Rexing R4 Pro (2K front plus three 1080p channels), $319.99 at rexing.com on the same date. These are Black Friday sale prices and can change when the sales end. Dealectric does not test units; every figure here is a maker's listing or a named tester's result.

  • Vantrue N5S, parked: at {price:vantrue-nexus-5s} on 2026-11-21 the camera is under $300, but by less than the $29.99 that Vantrue's hardwire kit costs. It fits the budget as a driving and rideshare camera, not as a parking-mode setup. {buy:vantrue-nexus-5s}
  • Vantrue N5 with kit: $265.99 + $29.99 = $295.98. It has the same four views as the N5S, with a 1080p rear instead of 1440p and a 512 GB card ceiling instead of 1 TB (Vantrue's figures).
  • Rexing R4 with kit: $259.99 + $29.99 = $289.98, which is $9.99 more than the R4-RD at $279.99 with its kit in the box. The R4 takes cards up to 256 GB and none is included.
  • Rexing C4 with kit: $199.99 + $39.99 = $239.98, before the GPS adapter. A 64 GB card is pre-installed.
  • Botslab G980H with kit: the $35.99 Botslab kit added to {price:botslab-g980h-4-camera-dash-cam} at the store, or to {after:botslab-g980h-4-camera-dash-cam} through our link, stays under $300 on 2026-11-21. A 128 GB card is in the box and it takes cards up to 512 GB. {buy:botslab-g980h-4-camera-dash-cam}
  • Rexing R4-RD parking draw: The Smart Home Hookup measured 0.4 Wh in a 30-minute parked test: 0.4 Wh ÷ 0.5 h = 0.8 W on average.

Which hardwire kit fits which camera

A dash cam records while parked only if it has power with the engine off. Digital Camera World's review of the N5S says the camera “will need to be hard-wired to your vehicle's 12 volt battery” and lists parking mode as “Yes, optional hardwire kit required”. The kit also cuts power at a set battery voltage so the camera cannot flatten the battery. Each maker names its own kit, and they are not interchangeable in the makers' listings.

CameraKit the maker names for itPrice (2026-11-21)Maker's stated limits
Vantrue N5S and N5Voltage Display Hardwire Kit$29.99 (list $34.99)12–24 V vehicles; cut-off at 11.6, 12 or 12.4 V (23.6, 24 or 24.4 V); shows battery voltage on a screen
Botslab G980H 4-ChannelType-C Hardwire Kit$35.99 (list $45.99)12–30 V input, 5 V / 2.4 A output, 9 ft cable; up to 24 hours of time-lapse or collision-triggered recording
Rexing R4-RDSmart Hardwire Kit, in the boxIncludedRexing's separate 360° Motion kit lists the R4-RD as an exception, so there is nothing to add
Rexing R4Type-C Smart Hardwire Kit$29.9912–30 V input, 5 V / 2 A output, 11.5 ft; cut-off at 11.8 V or 23.5 V; 8 fuse taps included
Rexing C4Smart Hardwire Kit with 360° Motion Detection$39.99 (list $59.99)Rexing says it supports “nearly all models except 4G LTE, R4-RD, and Multimedia Receiver units” and is “not supported for hybrid or pure electric vehicles”; the listing does not name the C4

Two fit details matter. Vantrue's and Rexing's cabin-facing or inward-turned cameras use infrared light, which helps inside the car; on the N5S, Ben Andrews found that “at night, very little will be visible through the car's side windows” and that “exterior coverage from the cabin cameras isn't great”. And the Rexing 360° Motion kit is for gasoline cars only, so a hybrid or electric car owner who wants outward side lenses with parking mode should look at the R4-RD or R4 instead of the C4.

Not recommended

Either outward side-lens camera, if the footage has to read plates at night. Both drew poor image verdicts from named testers. The Smart Home Hookup, in its 13-camera test published 2025-12-19, said of the R4-RD: “The Rexing was my least favorite image and was both oversaturated and overexposed”, and at night with both cars moving “the Rexing was just a blurry mess”. Vortex Radar, reviewing the 4-channel Botslab G980H on DashCamTalk on 2026-04-23, wrote “No HDR, so really struggles at night”, called the rear camera's video “subpar”, and said the parking G-sensor “has really low sensitivity”. The summary was “a crummy half-baked dashcam with a pair of side cams slapped onto the side”. The review also raised security concerns, which Botslab disputed in an update to the same post. Buy either for where its lenses point and what is in the box, not for image quality.

The Rexing R4 for parking mode. With its kit it costs $289.98, against $279.99 for the R4-RD, which adds a motion sensor and has the kit in the box. The R4 makes sense only if the camera will never be hardwired.
